sentences.text: The snout of this creature was laterally compressed, featuring a groove between the upper jaw bones to hold an enlarged lower tooth. A wedge-like projection extended from the front of the upper jaw, while the nostrils faced slightly forward and protruded ahead of the snout tip.
Its back armor consisted of thin dorsal plates with low ridges, while the smaller belly plates lacked these ridges entirely.

Llewellyn Ivor Price collected the single known specimen between 1947 and 1949 from the Serra da Galga Formation in Brazil. This fragmentary holotype includes a skull with five teeth and a partial skeleton with ribs and skin plates. After other related fossils were moved to a different genus, Peirosaurus remains known only from this one example.

Price named the genus Peirosaurus in 1955, establishing it as the type genus for the family Peirosauridae. The single species within this genus is Peirosaurus torminni. It belongs to the subfamily Peirosaurinae and is classified within the class Reptilia.
This reptile lived in Minas Gerais, southern Brazil, during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous. This period spans from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Scientists debate whether minor variations in skin plate thickness and tooth ridge details are enough to separate Peirosaurus from the genus Uberabasuchus.
